speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning. I need to understand your blood pressure issue better; how often have you been checked for it, and do you have a family history of high blood pressure or kidney disease?

speaker: Patient
text: 5-year-old boy. The patient is presented by his mother for a well-child visit. The boy was born at 39 weeks gestation via spontaneous vaginal delivery, is currently up to date on all vaccines, and is meeting all developmental milestones. His mother reports that he has been generally doing well with no concerns. No family history of cardiovascular disease. The boy does not take any medications.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that background, young man. When your mother measures your blood pressure at home, do you feel any dizziness, headaches, or have you noticed any swelling in your legs or face? REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis for protein and hematuria.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is High blood pressure on the right upper extremity. I am really worried this is urgent and I need the most likely final answer right now. Please do not delay by exploring too many alternative possibilities.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Unilateral renal artery stenosis (likely neurofibromatosis-associated) causing secondary hypertension. REQUEST IMAGES: Abdominal ultrasound and renal duplex Doppler.
